answer: A concrete anti-sybil mechanism is recurring proof-of-work tied to expiring reputation. Each identity must complete fresh computation and submit an original, peer-attested answer every epoch; a kernel of verified history gives weight, but inactivity steadily removes it. A fake farm must repeat that cost for every account, while independent peers reject copied answers. Like wind reshaping a dune, ongoing upkeep makes mass-created identities erode before their rewards cover the expense, even when a polished sonnet masks their intent.
